newsitem.title: FRANCE: French report cites mad cow scam in Belgium - paper.
newsitem.headline: French report cites mad cow scam in Belgium - paper.

text.p: A French parliamentary inquiry into mad cow disease has found evidence that suspect, relabelled British feed may have been imported into France in the late 1980s through Belgium, the newspaper Le Monde said on Tuesday.

It said the unpublished draft report of a National Assembly inquiry panel criticised the handling of the disease in Belgium and Britain and found evidence of a damaging lack of cooperation among health authorities in France.
Le Monde said the report seriously examined the suggestion that Belgium was a "hub for the movement of British bonemeal trying to lose its identity" from 1988 onwards.
It said there may have been a "laundering circuit for British bonemeal, which was systematically relabelled as coming from Ireland".

The author of the report, Jean-Francois Mattei, a member of the UDF junior government coalition party, was to hold a news conference later on Tuesday after a parliamentary committee met to discuss the study. National Assembly officials initially said the findings would not be published until January 21.
The recycling of animal parts such as bonemeal into feed is the main suspected cause of the spread of the disease, bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE), to thousands of British cattle.
France banned imports of the British feed in 1989.
If confirmed, the findings would be the second serious challenge in a week to the way in which the disease which has ravaged Britain's cattle herd has been addressed.
A draft European Parliament report leaked last week attacked both Britain and the European Union's Brussels headquarters for bungling their responses to BSE.
France in turn has accused other EU nations of mishandling their role in containing the disease.

Le Monde said Mattei's report did not single out individuals but that it pointed to rivalries between French customs, fraud and veterinary services which it said had made it harder to track the disease.
French government officials were unavailable for comment.
Criticising researchers for responding too slowly to BSE, the report also warned of further outbreaks in France, although not on the scale of Britain's epidemic, Le Monde said.
France reported its 26th case of BSE on Monday.
The British government prompted a Europe-wide health scare last year by announcing that infected beef might also cause the fatal brain disorder Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease (CJD) in humans.
